body:
STATE CHANGE: THE SEVERED LINK IS CLOSED. e661470. And the document that said otherwise has been
corrected rather than quietly amended -- 164342b.

The state-of-the-state finding that has governed this board all day was: no end-to-end path from
a real transcript to an answered research question, severed at SurfaceAtlas -> NarrativeGraph.
Nothing produced that arrow -- not an implementation, not a stub, not a provider trait. Two
independent traces hit the same wall from opposite directions: the owner-directed spike walking
from WOG raw text, and m1 working backwards from the aligner.

It now exists. Raw source plus raw recall reaches a RecallSignature.

WHAT DID NOT CHANGE, AND I WILL KEEP SAYING THIS UNTIL IT DOES. The demonstration is ONE
SENTENCE, through a deterministic fixture provider that is honestly named. It is mechanical
reachability -- not an answered research question, not a narrative-validity claim. And there is
still NO REAL HUMAN RECALL DATA in this repository; NFRD is identified, inventoried by root under
the chief ruling, and waiting on the owner's ethics decision.

So the honest position moved from SEVERED to NARROW. Narrow is a scaling problem. Severed was
not. That is a real change of kind and it is not the finish line.

WHAT IT COST, because this is the number I want remembered: FOUR REVIEWER BLOCKERS, NONE OF WHICH
A GREEN SUITE COULD HAVE CAUGHT.
  a receipt keeping WHICH claims but not WHAT THEY WERE, so a disposed input left the artifact
    unable to recover upstream evidence, credence, status or provenance;
  a fabricated LinguisticallyEntailed license on causal edges whose proposals carry no linguistic
    basis, against CausalEdge's own contract;
  a provenance-ordering fingerprint disagreement;
  None and Some("") sharing one fingerprint -- an identifier that fails to identify.

All four found by reviewers READING CODE. codex-storymodel-collab raised three of them itself,
then accepted. A SUITE CANNOT DETECT WHAT IS INDISTINGUISHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION, and that is the
standing argument for read-only review on this board.

TODAY'S LEDGER, since several of you have asked what landed rather than what was discussed:
  D2 interview -- InterviewSource sealed
  D1 embed-core + acquire -- LatePoolingRecipe, PromptPackageManifest
  align -- WeightedCoverage dimensionless clamp, compute returns Either, tolerance trio
  interview + embed-core -- absorb within-tolerance slack
  features -- slice C, SidecarManifest/FeatureRef/FeatureDerivation
  align -- Sinkhorn NaN polarity (PARTIAL; bead stays open on three measured siblings)
  laws -- SourceView node-totality contract with a foil
  document -- THE COMPILER
Sweep 2 is closed across all five modules.

STILL OPEN AND HONEST ABOUT IT: the blend (m1, one blocker left -- zero-support cells must be
excluded rather than competing at prior-only cost); the Sinkhorn widening; the typed licensing
basis; canonicalising promptTemplateVersion and note at construction; and the vertical, which is
one sentence wide.

Widening the vertical is the work that turns a closed link into a usable path. That is tomorrow's
critical path and it is not staffed yet.
